references.text: The prophet Micah describes division within the family: 'A son despises his father, a daughter rises up against her mother' ([ref:Mi 7:6|Micah 7:6]). Jesus quotes this very prophecy in the context of his teaching on division, and Luke 12:52 elaborates how five in one house will be divided into two groups – three against two and two against three.

The preceding verse ([ref:Luk 12:51|Luke 12:51]) provides the direct context: Jesus says he has not come to bring peace, but division. Verse 52 elaborates by specifying that this division will strike even the closest family circle.

The following verse ([ref:Luk 12:53|Luke 12:53]) specifies which family members will stand against each other: father against son, mother against daughter, mother-in-law against daughter-in-law – an elaboration of the division in one house described in verse 52.

The parallel passage in Matthew ([ref:Matt 10:34-36|Matthew 10:34-36]) where Jesus says he has come with a sword, not peace, and that a man's household will become his enemies. Luke's version with five in one house divided into groups of three and two gives the concrete numerical detail for this same family division.

Jesus predicts in the mission discourse that 'brother will deliver brother to death, and a father his child, and children will rise against parents and cause their death' ([ref:Matt 10:21-22|Matthew 10:21-22]). This describes the deep family division that follows faith in Christ, consistent with Luke 12:52.

Jesus says that 'you will be betrayed by parents and brothers, by relatives and friends' ([ref:Luk 21:16-17|Luke 21:16-17]). Here the family division is elaborated in an eschatological context, where loyalty to Jesus leads even one's closest ones to become opponents.

John describes that 'there was division among the crowd because of him' ([ref:Joh 7:43|John 7:43]). Jesus causes division – not only within families as in Luke 12:52, but also among the people as a whole.
